file: papers/pdf/Merton and Barber - 2004 - A Note on Serendipity as a Political Metaphor.pdf
about: A chapter tracing how 'serendipity' was used as a political metaphor in American commentary, from Johnson's view of the New Deal's unplanned windfalls to Reston's pejorative use for wishful, deceptive optimism.

candidates.label: Finding valued things while seeking others
candidates.definition: Serendipity is discovering interesting, delightful or valuable things while hunting for something quite different; the find is unexpected and unsought.
candidates.applies_when: Account describes coming across something valuable or pleasing while pursuing a different aim.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The valued result was the intended target of the search, or was anticipated in planning.

candidates.label: Chance or sagacity
candidates.definition: Drawing on Walpole's tale, serendipity involves discovering, by chance or by sagacity, wonderful things not sought, without being dismayed by misfortune.
candidates.applies_when: Account credits an unsought discovery to a mix of luck and the discoverer's shrewdness or perceptiveness.

candidates.label: Unplanned by-product windfalls
candidates.definition: Serendipity as unexpected positive consequences or 'velvet' that accompany a planned program but were not its purpose, such as unforeseen financial gains.
candidates.applies_when: Person reports a benefit that arose incidentally from an initiative undertaken for another reason.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The benefit was an explicit goal of the initiative.

candidates.label: Planning makes surprises visible
candidates.definition: A strong stress on planning makes unexpected benefits more conspicuous and more appreciated, because they stand out against what was planned.
candidates.applies_when: Account notes that an unexpected gain was noticed or valued because it departed from a deliberate plan.

candidates.label: Assisting things to turn up
candidates.definition: The contrast, via Mrs. Micawber, between expecting good things to turn up of themselves and actively helping to turn them up; the latter is endorsed over passive waiting.
candidates.applies_when: Person describes actively creating conditions for lucky breaks rather than waiting for them.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Person simply waits and hopes something will happen without acting.

candidates.label: Step-by-step piecemeal approach
candidates.definition: Pragmatic, piecemeal policymaking that does not anticipate each step's consequences far ahead, as opposed to grand comprehensive plans, implicitly leaves room for accidental success.
candidates.applies_when: Account describes proceeding incrementally without a fixed comprehensive plan, leaving openness to the unforeseen.

candidates.label: Morale boost from unexpected good luck
candidates.definition: Unexpected good luck works like a surprise gift that keeps people expectant and raises morale, offsetting unexpected bad luck.
candidates.applies_when: Person reports that a lucky surprise energized them, raised spirits or kept them motivated.

candidates.label: Different forms of serendipitous find
candidates.definition: Serendipitous discoveries can take different forms: a personality, an institution, or a broadening of one's mental horizon.
candidates.applies_when: Account describes unexpectedly encountering a person, organization, or new perspective.

candidates.label: Wishful 'something will turn up' optimism
candidates.definition: A critical use of serendipity as shallow, Micawberish opportunism: deception and self-deception, believing something will turn up while pretending all is well and ignoring real problems.
candidates.applies_when: Account invokes luck or 'things will work out' to avoid facing evident problems, rather than describing an actual unsought discovery.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: An actual unexpected discovery was noticed and acted upon with alertness and activity.

candidates.label: Serendipity as alertness and activity
candidates.definition: Among scientists, serendipity carries positive associations of alertness, imaginativeness and activity, as opposed to unearned increments or passive luck.
candidates.applies_when: Person narrates a lucky find as resulting from their own alertness, imagination or active effort.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Person frames the gain as an unearned windfall that simply happened to them.

candidates.label: Credit and unearned increments
candidates.definition: Unexpected benefits may be narrated as unearned increments of a plan, with planners credited for what they planned but not necessarily for the surprises.
candidates.applies_when: Account distinguishes between credit for planned results and windfalls that came without deliberate effort.
